title: How do we list numbers with a given digital root in a range?
description: Numbers between six hundred and seven hundred with digital root five, seven and three are listed by finding the first one and then adding nine each time. Keeko's doubt is that six hundred five has digital root five because it ends in five.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the first number with the wanted digital root, then keep adding nine, because adding nine does not change the root. Watch for students who read the digital root from the last digit instead of adding all the digits.

source: Between 600 and 700, list the numbers with digital root 5, 7 and 3
video_script.why: A learner finds the first number with a wanted digital root and then adds nine to list all the others in a range.
video_script.substitution: the book's own range, 600 to 700, and the digital roots 5, 7 and 3
video_script.anchor: a number line from 600 to 700 with the numbers of one digital root marked
video_script.wrong_answer: six hundred five has digital root five because it ends in five
video_script.wrong_move: reads the digital root from the last digit instead of adding all the digits
video_script.payoff_line: Each root has eleven numbers, starting at six hundred eight, six hundred one and six hundred six.

final_answer.value: Eleven numbers for each digital root, starting at 608, 601 and 606 and going up in nines
final_answer.spoken: each root has eleven numbers, starting at six hundred eight, six hundred one and six hundred six, and going up in nines

hold_back: Eleven numbers for each digital root, starting at 608, 601 and 606 and going up in nines
maths_rules: 600 has digit sum 6; 608 has digit sum 14, 1 + 4 = 5, root 5
adding 9 does not change the remainder on division by 9, so the digital root stays the same
the next number each time is 707, 700 and 705 for roots 5, 7, 3; 700 is the end of the range and is not between 600 and 700
video_script.design: One idea: find the first number with the wanted root, then add nine each time. Assumes the digital root and the digit sum. The number line from six hundred to seven hundred stays on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: title card Digital roots in a range; a number line from 600 to 700 with the words root 5, root 7, root 3 and a question mark

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the number line from 600 to 700 is drawn
marks.ask: the words root 5, root 7, root 3 appear above the line

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the numbers between six hundred and seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We have to list the numbers with digital root five. Then we do the same for seven and for three.
Which numbers are they?

beats.on_screen: the number line stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the digital root is a single digit from 1 to 9; two numbers with the same root leave the same remainder on division by 9

marks.range: the nine possible digital roots 1 to 9 appear above the number line
marks.same: two numbers with the same root are joined and the words same remainder on division by 9 appear

narration: <bookmark mark='range'/>A digital root is a single digit, from one to nine.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Two numbers with the same digital root leave the same remainder on division by nine.

beats.on_screen: Given: numbers between 600 and 700; digital roots 5, 7 and 3

marks.given: the range and the three roots are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers between six hundred and seven hundred, and the digital roots five, seven and three.

beats.on_screen: To find: all numbers in the range with each of these digital roots

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to list all the numbers in this range with each of the three roots.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Step one, find the first number above six hundred for each root. Six hundred has digit sum six.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Add eight and the digit sum is fourteen.
One plus four is five, so six hundred eight has digital root five.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Six hundred one has digit sum seven, so its digital root is seven.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Six hundred six has digit sum twelve. One plus two is three, so its digital root is three.

marks.nine: an arrow marked plus 9 appears between two numbers
marks.five: the root 5 list is written along the number line
marks.seven: the root 7 list is written along the number line
marks.three: the root 3 list is written along the number line
marks.count: each list is counted as 11 numbers and the next step reaches 700, the end of the range

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, adding nine leaves the remainder on division by nine the same. The digital root does not change.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Root five starts at six hundred eight. Then come six hundred seventeen and six hundred twenty six, up to six hundred ninety eight.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Root seven starts at six hundred one and goes up to six hundred ninety one.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Root three starts at six hundred six and goes up to six hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Adding nine once more reaches the end of the range, so each list has eleven numbers.

marks.check: 635 is picked from the root 5 list

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check six hundred thirty five from the first list.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Six plus three plus five is fourteen, and one plus four is five. It belongs.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Eleven numbers for each digital root, starting at 608, 601 and 606 and going up in nines
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each root has eleven numbers, starting at six hundred eight, six hundred one and six hundred six.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number 605
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 605 in the list for root 5; 6 + 0 + 5 = 11, 1 + 1 = 2 is written; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble with 605 in the root 5 list appears

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks six hundred five has digital root five because it ends in five.
<bookmark mark='add'/>But we add all the digits. Six plus zero plus five is eleven, and one plus one is two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The digital root of six hundred five is two. The last digit alone does not decide it.
